abbaye-de-beaulieu-en-rouergue.name: Beaulieu-en-Rouergue Abbey
abbaye-de-beaulieu-en-rouergue.description: Cistercian abbey founded in 1144 by monks from Clairvaux in the Seye valley, in the Rouergue. Sold as national property in 1791 and given to the state in 1973, it preserves its Gothic church and chapter house and now houses one of the finest collections of postwar French art (1945-1975).

abbaye-de-charroux.name: Charroux Abbey
abbaye-de-charroux.description: Benedictine abbey founded in 785 by Count Roger of Limoges under the protection of Charlemagne, famed for its relic of the Holy Prepuce and for a rotunda plan unique in France. All that survives is the octagonal lantern tower known as the Tour Charlemagne, 37 metres high, along with fragments of the cloister and chapter house.

abbaye-de-cluny.name: Cluny Abbey
abbaye-de-cluny.description: Benedictine abbey founded in 910 by Duke William I of Aquitaine, cradle of the Cluniac order, which grew to include some one thousand monasteries across Europe. Its Cluny III abbey church, begun in 1088, was the largest church in Christendom until St Peter's in Rome was rebuilt; sold as national property and largely demolished after 1798, only the Eau Bénite bell tower and south transept survive.

abbaye-de-la-sauve-majeure.name: La Sauve-Majeure Abbey
abbaye-de-la-sauve-majeure.description: Benedictine abbey founded in 1079 by Gérard de Corbie, a major waypoint on the pilgrim routes to Santiago de Compostela and listed for that role as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1998. Ruined since the 19th century, it preserves its Romanesque chevet and more than eighty carved capitals, one of the richest ensembles of Romanesque sculpture in the Gironde.

abbaye-de-montmajour.name: Montmajour Abbey
abbaye-de-montmajour.description: Benedictine abbey founded in 948 near Arles, which grew into one of the wealthiest in Provence, as its Notre-Dame abbey church (1130-1182), Romanesque cloister, Sainte-Croix chapel and troglodyte Saint-Pierre hermitage still attest. Abandoned after the Revolution, it inspired numerous drawings by Van Gogh in 1888.

abbaye-du-bec-hellouin.name: Bec Abbey
abbaye-du-bec-hellouin.description: Benedictine abbey founded in 1034 by Herluin, whose school, led first by Lanfranc and then by Anselm, both future archbishops of Canterbury, became renowned across medieval Europe. Turned into a military horse depot under Napoleon, it regained a monastic community in 1948; visitors can see the 15th-century Saint-Nicolas tower and the cloister.

abbaye-du-mont-saint-michel.name: Mont-Saint-Michel Abbey
abbaye-du-mont-saint-michel.description: Sanctuary founded around 708 by Bishop Aubert of Avranches, which became a Benedictine abbey in 966, built atop a rocky islet exposed to the bay's powerful tides. The Merveille, a Gothic ensemble of stacked halls built between 1211 and 1228, was added to the 11th-century Romanesque church; a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1979, the abbey has hosted the Monastic Fraternities of Jerusalem since 2001.

abbaye-du-thoronet.name: Thoronet Abbey
abbaye-du-thoronet.description: Cistercian abbey founded in 1146, the oldest of the 'three Provençal sisters' alongside Sénanque and Silvacane, built of local stone between 1160 and 1180. UNESCO regards it as the most accomplished example of Cistercian architecture; restored between 1985 and 1990, it now serves as a museum and concert venue.

alignements-de-carnac.name: Carnac Stones
alignements-de-carnac.description: Nearly 3,000 standing stones erected around 2500 BC over some 4 kilometres, arranged in three main alignments — Ménec, Kermario and Kerlescan. Their purpose remains uncertain and has prompted many theories; the site joined the UNESCO World Heritage list in 2025.

arc-de-triomphe.name: Arc de Triomphe
arc-de-triomphe.description: Triumphal arch commissioned by Napoleon in 1806 and completed in 1836 at the top of the Champs-Élysées. It shelters the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, and its rooftop terrace overlooks the twelve avenues radiating from Place de l'Étoile.

archea-archeologie-en-pays-de-france.name: ARCHÉA, Archaeology in Pays de France
archea-archeologie-en-pays-de-france.description: Archaeology museum of the Roissy Pays de France area, opened in Louvres in 2010. Its displays come from local excavations, notably the medieval castle of Orville and the potters' workshops of Fosses, spanning two millennia of life north of Paris.

arenes-de-lutece.name: Arènes de Lutèce
arenes-de-lutece.description: Remains of a 1st-century Gallo-Roman amphitheatre in the Latin Quarter, which could seat around 15,000 spectators for plays and combat games. Rediscovered in 1869 during building works, the arena now serves as a public square.

basilique-cathedrale-de-saint-denis.name: Basilica of Saint-Denis
basilique-cathedrale-de-saint-denis.description: Abbey church rebuilt from 1135 under Abbot Suger and regarded as the birthplace of Gothic architecture. Necropolis of the French monarchy, it holds more than seventy recumbent effigies and tombs, from Dagobert to Louis XVI and Marie-Antoinette.

basilique-du-sacre-coeur-de-montmartre.name: Sacré-Cœur Basilica
basilique-du-sacre-coeur-de-montmartre.description: Romano-Byzantine basilica crowning the Montmartre hill, begun in 1875 as a national vow and consecrated in 1919. Its white domes are a Paris landmark, and the esplanade in front offers a sweeping panorama over the city.

bourse-de-commerce-pinault-collection.name: Bourse de Commerce – Pinault Collection
bourse-de-commerce-pinault-collection.description: Contemporary art museum opened in 2021 in the former Paris commodities exchange, a circular building crowned by a 19th-century glass-and-iron dome. Redesigned by Tadao Ando, it presents rotating exhibitions from François Pinault's collection.

cairn-de-barnenez.name: Barnenez Cairn
cairn-de-barnenez.description: Neolithic cairn built around 4700 BC, one of the oldest monuments in Europe, 75 metres long and containing eleven passage graves built in two phases. Threatened by a quarry in 1955, it was saved through the intervention of archaeologist Pierre-Roland Giot.

cathedrale-de-besancon-et-son-horloge-as.name: Besançon Cathedral and Astronomical Clock
cathedrale-de-besancon-et-son-horloge-as.description: Besançon's Saint-Jean Cathedral, whose astronomical clock was built between 1857 and 1860 by clockmaker Auguste-Lucien Vérité. Its roughly 30,000 parts drive 122 dials and automatons displaying hours, tides, eclipses and religious feast days from around the world.

cathedrale-et-tresor-de-chartres.name: Chartres Cathedral and Treasury
cathedrale-et-tresor-de-chartres.description: Gothic cathedral built largely within the thirty years following the fire of 1194 and consecrated in 1260, famed for its 13th-century stained-glass windows and their inimitable blue. Its treasury, reopened in 2024, holds the Veil of the Virgin (Sancta Camisia), venerated since the 9th century.

cathedrale-notre-dame-de-paris.name: Notre-Dame Cathedral
cathedrale-notre-dame-de-paris.description: Gothic cathedral on the Île de la Cité, built between 1163 and 1345, famed for its twin-towered façade, rose windows and flying buttresses. Damaged by fire in 2019, it reopened to visitors in December 2024 after restoration.

chapelle-des-moines-de-berze-la-ville.name: Monks' Chapel of Berzé-la-Ville
chapelle-des-moines-de-berze-la-ville.description: Romanesque chapel of the priory given in 1100 to Hugh of Semur, abbot of Cluny, as a retreat residence. Its early-12th-century murals, rediscovered in 1887 beneath whitewash, rank among the finest surviving examples of Cluniac art.

chapelle-expiatoire.name: Expiatory Chapel
chapelle-expiatoire.description: Neoclassical chapel built between 1815 and 1826 for Louis XVIII on the former Madeleine cemetery, where Louis XVI and Marie-Antoinette were buried after their execution. Designed by Pierre Fontaine, it is a memorial to victims of the Revolution.

chateau-d-angers.name: Château d'Angers
chateau-d-angers.description: Fortress built between 1230 and 1242 for Saint Louis and his mother Blanche of Castile, ringed by seventeen towers and more than 800 metres of ramparts overlooking the Maine river. Since 1954 it has housed the Apocalypse Tapestry, woven between 1373 and 1380 for Louis I of Anjou, one of the largest medieval tapestries to survive.

chateau-d-assier.name: Château d'Assier
chateau-d-assier.description: Renaissance château built between 1518 and 1535 by Galiot de Genouillac, master of artillery under François I, on the foundations of a medieval fortress. Largely demolished in the 18th century, only the west wing survives, decorated with a carved frieze celebrating its builder's military exploits.

chateau-d-aulteribe.name: Château d'Aulteribe
chateau-d-aulteribe.description: Stronghold fortified in 1467 by Charles Motier de La Fayette, remodelled in the 19th century in neo-Gothic taste by Joseph de Pierre and his wife Marie-Pauline Onslow. Bequeathed to the state in 1954, the château preserves furniture and tapestries spanning the 15th to 19th centuries.

chateau-d-azay-le-rideau.name: Château d'Azay-le-Rideau
chateau-d-azay-le-rideau.description: Renaissance château built between 1518 and 1527 for Gilles Berthelot, a treasurer to François I, partly raised on piles within the bed of the Indre river. Confiscated by the king after its owner's disgrace, it is today one of the most visited châteaux of the Loire.

chateau-d-if.name: Château d'If
chateau-d-if.description: Fortress built between 1524 and 1531 on the orders of François I to defend Marseille's harbour, converted into a state prison as early as the mid-16th century. Alexandre Dumas imprisoned Edmond Dantès here in The Count of Monte Cristo, making this small rocky island famous worldwide.

chateau-d-oiron.name: Château d'Oiron
chateau-d-oiron.description: Renaissance château of the Gouffier family, notably Claude Gouffier, Grand Squire of France, famed for its 55-metre painted gallery illustrating the Trojan War. State property since 1946, it has hosted the Curios & Mirabilia contemporary art collection, devised by Jean-Hubert Martin, since 1993.

chateau-de-bouges.name: Château de Bouges
chateau-de-bouges.description: Small neoclassical château built in 1765 for Charles Leblanc de Marnaval, in the spirit of the Petit Trianon. Bequeathed in 1967 with its 1,600 pieces of furniture by Henri Viguier, president of the Bazar de l'Hôtel de Ville department store, it is set in an 80-hectare park laid out by Henri and Achille Duchêne.

chateau-de-bussy-rabutin.name: Château de Bussy-Rabutin
chateau-de-bussy-rabutin.description: Fourteenth-century château remodelled during the Renaissance, where the writer Roger de Bussy-Rabutin, exiled by order of Louis XIV after his scandalous Histoire amoureuse des Gaules, spent seventeen years commissioning more than five hundred portraits of the court. His apartments form a satirical gallery of the Sun King's reign.

chateau-de-carrouges.name: Château de Carrouges
chateau-de-carrouges.description: Château of the Blosset and Le Veneur families, built in red and black brick from the 14th century onward and surrounded by moats. Its Louis XII-style gatehouse was commissioned by Cardinal Jean Le Veneur; state property since 1936, it is now managed by the Centre des monuments nationaux.

chateau-de-castelnau-bretenoux.name: Château de Castelnau-Bretenoux
chateau-de-castelnau-bretenoux.description: Red sandstone fortress of the lords of Castelnau, vassals of the counts of Toulouse, built from the 12th century onward on a promontory above the Dordogne valley. Ruined by a fire in 1851, it was restored over thirty years by the opera singer Jean Mouliérat, who bequeathed the château and its collections to the state.

chateau-de-champs-sur-marne.name: Château de Champs-sur-Marne
chateau-de-champs-sur-marne.description: Early 18th-century château east of Paris, once rented by Madame de Pompadour, noted for its rococo interiors, chinoiserie décors and period furniture. Its 85-hectare park combines French formal gardens with landscaped grounds.

chateau-de-chareil-cintrat.name: Château de Chareil-Cintrat
chateau-de-chareil-cintrat.description: Former Bourbon fief remodelled during the Renaissance by Claude Morin, an army administrator who made his fortune during the Italian campaigns. The staircase and a first-floor chamber preserve 16th-century murals depicting the gods of Olympus and an astrological cycle.

chateau-de-chateaudun.name: Château de Châteaudun
chateau-de-chateaudun.description: Fortress founded in 1171, whose 31-metre cylindrical keep, among the oldest in France, dates from 1180. Jean de Dunois, a companion-in-arms of Joan of Arc, had a Gothic residential wing and the Sainte-Chapelle built there between 1452 and 1468; the chapel preserves some fifteen statues of saints.

chateau-de-coucy.name: Château de Coucy
chateau-de-coucy.description: Fortress built from 1225 by Enguerrand III de Coucy, whose 54-metre cylindrical keep, the tallest in Europe, embodied the lord of Coucy's motto: 'King I am not, nor prince, nor duke, nor count either. I am the lord of Coucy.' It was blown up in 1917 by the retreating German army.

chateau-de-fougeres-sur-bievre.name: Château de Fougères-sur-Bièvre
chateau-de-fougeres-sur-bievre.description: Château rebuilt from 1475 to 1483 for Pierre de Refuge, a treasurer to Louis XI, on the ruins of a fortress destroyed during the Hundred Years' War. A Renaissance gallery with flattened arches was added in the 16th century around the medieval keep, which still stands.

chateau-de-gramont.name: Château de Gramont
chateau-de-gramont.description: Thirteenth-century fortress that passed from Simon de Montfort to the Montaut family, given a Renaissance wing with mullioned windows and a ribbed spiral staircase between 1535 and 1545. Donated to the Centre des monuments nationaux by Monsieur and Madame Dichamp, it retains its original furnishings.

chateau-de-la-motte-tilly.name: Château de la Motte-Tilly
chateau-de-la-motte-tilly.description: Château built from 1754 for the abbé Terray, later controller-general of finances under Louis XV, and kept in the same family until 1972. Entirely refurnished in the 20th century by the Marquise de Maillé, who bequeathed it with its 1,000-hectare estate to the state, on condition that it remain furnished but unlived in.

chateau-de-maisons.name: Château de Maisons
chateau-de-maisons.description: Château built by François Mansart between 1630 and 1646 for René de Longueil, regarded as a founding work of French classical architecture. Its monumental staircase and carved stone interiors influenced the design of Versailles.

chateau-de-montal.name: Château de Montal
chateau-de-montal.description: Renaissance château built between 1519 and 1534 by Jeanne de Balsac d'Entraygues in memory of her son Robert, killed in war in 1523, with an Italian-inspired straight staircase and carved busts of her family. Stripped and sold off in 1880, it was bought back and restored between 1908 and 1913 by the industrialist Maurice Fenaille, who donated it to the state.

chateau-de-pierrefonds.name: Château de Pierrefonds
chateau-de-pierrefonds.description: Fortress begun in 1396 for Louis d'Orléans, dismantled on the orders of Louis XIII in 1617 and left in ruins for two centuries. Napoleon III entrusted its restoration to Eugène Viollet-le-Duc from 1857, who reimagined it as a showcase of medieval architecture.

chateau-de-puyguilhem.name: Château de Puyguilhem
chateau-de-puyguilhem.description: Small Renaissance château built between 1513 and 1535 by Mondot de La Marthonie, first president of the parliament of Guyenne, as a hunting residence inspired by the châteaux of the Loire. Left to decay and then expropriated in 1938, it was restored by the state over some twenty years.

chateau-de-rambouillet.name: Château de Rambouillet
chateau-de-rambouillet.description: Royal then presidential residence set in a vast wooded park, where King François I died in 1547. The visit takes in 18th-century apartments, Marie-Antoinette's dairy and the shell-lined cottage built for the Princess de Lamballe.

chateau-de-sceaux-musee-departemental.name: Château de Sceaux
chateau-de-sceaux-musee-departemental.description: Departmental museum in a 19th-century château at the heart of the estate created for Colbert. Paintings, furniture and Sceaux ceramics evoke the history of the domain and life in Île-de-France, set in a park designed by André Le Nôtre.

chateau-de-talcy.name: Château de Talcy
chateau-de-talcy.description: Château purchased in 1517 by the Florentine banker Bernard Salviati, whose daughter Cassandre, whom Pierre de Ronsard met in 1545, inspired his poem 'Mignonne, allons voir si la rose...'. Catherine de' Medici and Charles IX held a conference between Catholics and Protestants there in 1562.

chateau-de-villeneuve-lembron.name: Château de Villeneuve-Lembron
chateau-de-villeneuve-lembron.description: Château built in the late 15th century for Rigaud d'Aureille, chamberlain to Louis XI and then Charles VIII, combining defensive tradition — four round towers and wide moats — with Renaissance comfort. Its rooms preserve lively painted murals, including a caricature portrait of its builder.

chateau-de-vincennes.name: Château de Vincennes
chateau-de-vincennes.description: Medieval royal residence on the eastern edge of Paris, with a 52-metre keep, the tallest of its kind in Europe, and a Sainte-Chapelle begun in 1379. French kings lived here before Versailles; the keep later became a state prison.

chateau-de-voltaire-a-ferney.name: Voltaire's Château at Ferney
chateau-de-voltaire-a-ferney.description: Residence where Voltaire settled in 1758 and lived until his death in 1778, after rebuilding the château and turning the village into a thriving community of 1,500 people through workshops producing watches and silk. Restored between 2015 and 2018, it now displays his apartments and the chapel he built in 1761.

chateau-ducal-de-cadillac.name: Château de Cadillac
chateau-ducal-de-cadillac.description: Château built between 1598 and 1634 for Jean-Louis de Nogaret de La Valette, Duke of Épernon and a favourite of Henri III, in a style already anticipating 17th-century classicism. Painted ceilings, monumental fireplaces and tapestries make up its decor; used as a women's prison from 1822 to 1951, it is now managed by the Centre des monuments nationaux.

chateau-et-remparts-de-la-cite-de-carcas.name: Carcassonne Castle and Ramparts
chateau-et-remparts-de-la-cite-de-carcas.description: Fortified city of Gallo-Roman origin, ringed by a double wall nearly 3 kilometres long with 52 towers, which surrendered to Simon de Montfort during the Albigensian Crusade in 1209. Restored from the 1850s onward by Eugène Viollet-le-Duc, it has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1997.

chateau-musee-de-nemours.name: Nemours Castle Museum
chateau-musee-de-nemours.description: Twelfth-century castle in the centre of Nemours, saved by local artists and opened as a museum in 1903. Its collections centre on fine arts of the late 19th and early 20th centuries, including works by sculptor Justin-Chrysostome Sanson.

collections-de-la-fondation-de-coubertin.name: Collections of the Coubertin Foundation
collections-de-la-fondation-de-coubertin.description: Museum of the Coubertin Foundation in the Chevreuse valley, devoted to sculpture around the figure of Joseph Bernard and to fine craftsmanship. Bronzes are displayed outdoors in the Jardin des Bronzes, beside the estate's renowned workshops.

conciergerie.name: Conciergerie
conciergerie.description: Surviving part of the medieval royal palace on the Île de la Cité, later the Revolution's most notorious prison, where Marie-Antoinette was held before her execution. The Gothic Hall of the Men-at-Arms dates from the early 14th century.

ecomusee-94260.name: Grand-Orly Seine Bièvre Ecomuseum
ecomusee-94260.description: Community museum founded in 1979 in the former Cottinville farm in Fresnes, documenting everyday life and social change in the southern suburbs of Paris. It collects residents' objects and memories and presents society-focused exhibitions.

europa-experience.name: Europa Experience
europa-experience.description: Visitor centre of the European Parliament on Place de la Madeleine, opened in 2022. Interactive displays, a 360-degree cinema and role-play games explain how the European Union works and what it does in daily life.

fondation-arp.name: Arp Foundation
fondation-arp.description: House and studios of artists Jean Arp and Sophie Taeuber-Arp in Clamart, built in 1929 to Taeuber-Arp's own design. Rooms and garden display the couple's sculptures, reliefs and works on paper, kept close to their original arrangement.

hotel-de-la-marine.name: Hôtel de la Marine
hotel-de-la-marine.description: Ange-Jacques Gabriel's 18th-century palace on Place de la Concorde housed the royal furniture storehouse, then the Navy Ministry for two centuries. Reopened in 2021, it displays restored period apartments and grand salons overlooking the square.

la-cinematheque-francaise.name: La Cinémathèque française
la-cinematheque-francaise.description: Film archive and museum founded in 1936 by Henri Langlois, housed in a Frank Gehry building in Bercy. Its Musée Méliès traces cinema history through cameras, costumes and magic-lantern devices, alongside daily screenings and exhibitions.

la-maison-elysee.name: La Maison Élysée
la-maison-elysee.description: Visitor space opposite the Élysée Palace at 88 rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré, combining a small museum, boutique and tea room. Objects, portraits and a 3D film retrace the palace's history from the 1722 Hôtel d'Évreux to the present-day presidency.

le-plateau-frac-ile-de-france.name: Le Plateau – Frac Île-de-France
le-plateau-frac-ile-de-france.description: Exhibition space of the Fonds régional d'art contemporain d'Île-de-France, in the Buttes-Chaumont district of the 19th arrondissement. It presents several contemporary art shows a year, drawing on the regional collection and emerging or international artists.

maison-de-balzac.name: Balzac's House
maison-de-balzac.description: The writer's modest house in Passy, the only one of Balzac's Paris homes still standing, where he lived from 1840 to 1847 and corrected La Comédie humaine. Manuscripts, portraits and his famous turquoise-studded cane evoke his life and work.

maison-de-victor-hugo.name: Victor Hugo's House
maison-de-victor-hugo.description: The apartment on Place des Vosges where Victor Hugo lived from 1832 to 1848, now a museum. Drawings, manuscripts, portraits and the Chinese-style salon he created for Juliette Drouet retrace the writer's life from childhood to exile.

maison-des-jardies.name: Jardies House
maison-des-jardies.description: A former vintner's house in Sèvres where Balzac lived from 1837 to 1840 and where Léon Gambetta died in 1882. Run by the Centre des monuments nationaux, it keeps Gambetta's rooms as they were, with a Bartholdi monument in the garden.

maison-musee-maurice-ravel.name: Maurice Ravel House-Museum
maison-musee-maurice-ravel.description: Le Belvédère, the small house in Montfort-l'Amaury where Maurice Ravel lived from 1921 to 1937 and composed Boléro among other works. Its rooms preserve his furniture, mechanical toys and decor exactly as the composer arranged them.

maison-natale-de-louis-braille.name: Louis Braille's Birthplace
maison-natale-de-louis-braille.description: The family home in Coupvray where Louis Braille was born in 1809, with the saddlery workshop where he lost his sight as a child. The museum retraces his life and the invention of the raised-dot alphabet used by blind readers worldwide.

memorial-de-la-shoah.name: Shoah Memorial
memorial-de-la-shoah.description: France's central Holocaust memorial and museum, in the Marais. The Wall of Names lists the 76,000 Jews deported from France, while a permanent exhibition and a major documentation centre trace the Shoah and Jewish life in Europe.

memorial-de-la-shoah-de-drancy.name: Drancy Shoah Memorial
memorial-de-la-shoah-de-drancy.description: Memorial and museum opened in 2012 facing the Cité de la Muette, the housing estate that served as the Drancy internment camp from 1941 to 1944, from which some 63,000 Jews were deported. Its exhibition documents the camp's history and daily life.

mus-musee-d-histoire-urbaine-et-sociale-.name: MUS – Suresnes Museum of Urban and Social History
mus-musee-d-histoire-urbaine-et-sociale-.description: Museum of urban and social history housed in the former Suresnes-Longchamp railway station. It tells how the town was transformed in the 20th century, notably by Henri Sellier's garden city and the pioneering open-air school.

musee.name: Nogent-sur-Marne Intercommunal Museum
musee.description: Local history museum for the Marne riverbanks, telling how boating, bathing and riverside guinguettes made Nogent a centre of Parisian Sunday leisure from the 19th century. Paintings, posters and postcards document the surrounding communes.

musee-adrien-mentienne.name: Adrien Mentienne Museum
musee-adrien-mentienne.description: Bry-sur-Marne's municipal museum, named after a local historian and mayor. Alongside local history collections, it holds one of France's most important collections on Louis Daguerre, inventor of the daguerreotype, who spent his last years in Bry.

musee-alfred-bonno.name: Alfred Bonno Museum
musee-alfred-bonno.description: Chelles' archaeology museum, reopened in 2026 in fully redesigned spaces. Finds from local digs run from Palaeolithic flint tools to the Merovingian era, including rare early-medieval textiles linked to Queen Bathild and the royal abbey of Chelles.

musee-archeologique-departemental-du-val.name: Val-d'Oise Archaeology Museum (MADVO)
musee-archeologique-departemental-du-val.description: The Val-d'Oise departmental archaeology museum, in the Vexin village of Guiry. Its chronological displays span prehistory to the 20th century, with finds from the Gallo-Roman site of Genainville and France's largest collection of Merovingian steles.

musee-belmondo-et-de-la-sculpture-figura.name: Paul Belmondo Museum
musee-belmondo-et-de-la-sculpture-figura.description: Museum in the 18th-century Château Buchillot devoted to sculptor Paul Belmondo (1898-1982), a leading figure of 20th-century figurative sculpture. It shows his marbles, bronzes, medals and drawings, donated to Boulogne-Billancourt by his children.

musee-bossuet.name: Bossuet Museum
musee-bossuet.description: Meaux's fine-arts museum in the former episcopal palace beside the cathedral, named after Bossuet, the city's celebrated 17th-century bishop and preacher. It shows paintings and sculpture from the 16th to 19th centuries, with a mitre-shaped garden attributed to Le Nôtre.

musee-bourdelle.name: Bourdelle Museum
musee-bourdelle.description: The Montparnasse studios and gardens where sculptor Antoine Bourdelle, a pupil and assistant of Rodin, lived and worked. Plasters, marbles and monumental bronzes such as Hercules the Archer are shown in the preserved workshops and a modern extension.

musee-carnavalet-histoire-de-paris.name: Carnavalet Museum
musee-carnavalet-histoire-de-paris.description: The museum of the history of Paris, set in two Marais mansions including the Hôtel Carnavalet, once home to the letter-writer Madame de Sévigné. Its collections run from prehistoric canoes to the French Revolution and the modern city.

musee-cernuschi-musee-des-arts-de-l-asie.name: Cernuschi Museum
musee-cernuschi-musee-des-arts-de-l-asie.description: The City of Paris's Asian art museum, built around the collection of banker Henri Cernuschi in his mansion beside Parc Monceau. It is noted for its ancient Chinese bronzes and a monumental Japanese Buddha brought from Meguro.

musee-cognacq-jay-musee-du-xviiie-siecle.name: Cognacq-Jay Museum
musee-cognacq-jay-musee-du-xviiie-siecle.description: An intimate museum of 18th-century art in the Hôtel Donon in the Marais, formed from the collection of Ernest Cognacq, founder of La Samaritaine department store: paintings by Boucher, Fragonard and Chardin, pastels, porcelain and furniture.

musee-curie.name: Curie Museum
musee-curie.description: Housed in Marie Curie's former laboratory at the Radium Institute, where she worked until her death in 1934, the museum preserves her office and chemistry lab and traces the history of radioactivity and a family awarded five Nobel Prizes.

musee-d-archeologie-nationale-des-origin.name: National Archaeology Museum
musee-d-archeologie-nationale-des-origin.description: France's national archaeology museum occupies the royal château of Saint-Germain-en-Laye, rebuilt under François I. Its collections run from the Palaeolithic to the early Middle Ages and include the 25,000-year-old Lady of Brassempouy.

musee-d-art-contemporain-du-val-de-marne.name: Val-de-Marne Museum of Contemporary Art (MAC VAL)
musee-d-art-contemporain-du-val-de-marne.description: Opened in 2005 in Vitry-sur-Seine, MAC VAL was the first museum devoted solely to contemporary art made in France since the 1950s. Its collection is shown in regularly renewed displays, alongside temporary exhibitions and a sculpture garden.

musee-d-art-et-d-histoire.name: Meudon Museum of Art and History
musee-d-art-et-d-histoire.description: Meudon's museum of art and history occupies the town's oldest house, once home to royal surgeon Ambroise Paré and later to Molière's widow Armande Béjart. It covers local history and landscape painting, with 20th-century sculpture in the garden.

musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-de-l-hopital-s.name: Sainte-Anne Hospital Museum of Art and History
musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-de-l-hopital-s.description: A museum inside the Sainte-Anne psychiatric hospital in the 14th arrondissement, presenting the hospital's collection of works made by patients, assembled since the mid-20th century — a major ensemble of art brut — alongside temporary exhibitions.

musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-du-judaisme.name: Museum of Jewish Art and History
musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-du-judaisme.description: Housed in the 17th-century Hôtel de Saint-Aignan in the Marais, the museum traces Jewish art and history from the Middle Ages to today, with ceremonial objects, archives of the Dreyfus affair and works by Chagall, Modigliani and Soutine.

musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-louis-senlecq.name: Louis Senlecq Museum of Art and History
musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-louis-senlecq.description: L'Isle-Adam's museum of art and history, in an 18th-century mansion, holds one of the finest collections of the landscape painter Jules Dupré, a Barbizon-school figure who kept his studio in the town, alongside works on local heritage.

musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-paul-eluard.name: Paul Éluard Museum of Art and History
musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-paul-eluard.description: Saint-Denis's museum of art and history is set in a former Carmelite convent where Louis XV's daughter Louise was a nun. Collections range from the convent's restored cells to the Paris Commune of 1871 and the poet Paul Éluard, born in the town.

musee-d-art-moderne-de-la-ville-de-paris.name: Paris Museum of Modern Art
musee-d-art-moderne-de-la-ville-de-paris.description: The City of Paris's modern art museum, in the east wing of the 1937 Palais de Tokyo, spans 20th- and 21st-century art from Fauvism to today, with major works by Matisse, Delaunay and Dufy, including his vast mural 'La Fée Électricité'.

musee-d-ennery.name: D'Ennery Museum
musee-d-ennery.description: A house-museum on avenue Foch attached to the Musée Guimet, preserving the Japanese and Chinese art collected by Clémence d'Ennery in the 19th century — netsuke, ceramics and fantastic creatures — in its original Second Empire interiors.

musee-d-histoire-locale-memoire-de-la-vi.name: Rueil-Malmaison Museum of Local History
musee-d-histoire-locale-memoire-de-la-vi.description: A local history museum in Rueil-Malmaison's former 19th-century town hall, covering the town from its origins to today, with figurine displays of Napoleon's Grande Armée and mementoes of Empress Joséphine, who lived at nearby Malmaison.

musee-d-orsay.name: Musée d'Orsay
musee-d-orsay.description: Set in the former Orsay railway station, built for the 1900 World's Fair, the museum holds the world's richest collection of Impressionist and Post-Impressionist painting — Monet, Renoir, Degas, Van Gogh — and French art from 1848 to 1914.

musee-daubigny.name: Daubigny Museum
musee-daubigny.description: A museum in the 17th-century Manoir des Colombières in Auvers-sur-Oise devoted to Charles-François Daubigny, a forerunner of Impressionism, with works by his circle and the painters of the Oise valley, plus collections of naïve and feline-themed art.

musee-de-l-air-et-de-l-espace.name: Air and Space Museum
musee-de-l-air-et-de-l-espace.description: One of the world's oldest aviation museums, founded in 1919 at Paris–Le Bourget airport. Its collection runs from pioneer-era flying machines to Concorde airliners and Ariane rockets, displayed in the 1937 terminal building and on the tarmac.

musee-de-l-armee.name: Army Museum
musee-de-l-armee.description: France's military history museum at Les Invalides, the veterans' complex built by Louis XIV. Its collections span medieval armour to the two World Wars, and the golden-domed church shelters the tomb of Napoleon I.

musee-de-l-ecole-de-barbizon-auberge-gan.name: Museum of the Barbizon School – Auberge Ganne
musee-de-l-ecole-de-barbizon-auberge-gan.description: The former Ganne inn in Barbizon, where landscape painters lodged from the 1820s, keeps walls and cupboards covered with their painted decorations. The museum recounts the school led by Millet and Théodore Rousseau at the edge of Fontainebleau forest.

musee-de-l-ecole-nationale-superieure-de.name: Museum of the École Nationale Supérieure des Beaux-Arts
musee-de-l-ecole-nationale-superieure-de.description: The collection of France's historic fine-arts school holds some 450,000 works, from old-master drawings and prints to Prix de Rome student pieces, shown in temporary exhibitions in the school's buildings on the Left Bank.

musee-de-l-histoire-vivante.name: Museum of Living History
musee-de-l-histoire-vivante.description: A museum of French social and working-class history, founded in 1937 and set in a mansion in Montreuil's Parc Montreau. Photographs, prints and objects trace the labour movement and political struggles from the Revolution to today.

musee-de-l-hotel-dieu.name: Museum of the Hôtel-Dieu
musee-de-l-hotel-dieu.description: Mantes-la-Jolie's fine-arts museum occupies the listed former chapel of the town's Hôtel-Dieu hospital, renovated in 2018. It holds France's most important public collection of works by the Neo-Impressionist painter Maximilien Luce.

musee-de-l-institut-du-monde-arabe.name: Arab World Institute Museum
musee-de-l-institut-du-monde-arabe.description: The Arab World Institute's museum surveys the arts and civilisations of the Arab world, from pre-Islamic antiquity to contemporary creation, inside Jean Nouvel's landmark 1987 building with its light-filtering geometric facade.

musee-de-l-orangerie-des-tuileries.name: Musée de l'Orangerie
musee-de-l-orangerie-des-tuileries.description: A former Tuileries orangery now displaying Monet's monumental Water Lilies cycle in two oval rooms designed for it, alongside the Walter-Guillaume collection of Renoir, Cézanne, Matisse, Picasso and Modigliani.

musee-de-la-batellerie.name: Museum of Inland Waterways
musee-de-la-batellerie.description: Set in the Château du Prieuré overlooking Conflans-Sainte-Honorine, the historic capital of France's barge people, this museum traces inland waterway navigation through ship models, tools and documents on canals, towing and river trade.

musee-de-la-chasse-et-de-la-nature.name: Museum of Hunting and Nature
musee-de-la-chasse-et-de-la-nature.description: In two Marais mansions, the Hôtel de Guénégaud and Hôtel de Mongelas, this museum explores the relationship between humans and animals, mixing old-master paintings, taxidermy, historic weapons and contemporary art.

musee-de-la-franc-maconnerie.name: Museum of Freemasonry
musee-de-la-franc-maconnerie.description: At the headquarters of the Grand Orient de France on Rue Cadet, this museum recounts three centuries of Freemasonry in France through ritual objects, aprons, lodge regalia and documents linked to celebrated masons such as Voltaire and La Fayette.

musee-de-la-gendarmerie.name: National Gendarmerie Museum
musee-de-la-gendarmerie.description: The national museum of the French Gendarmerie, opened in 2015 beside the officers' academy in Melun, retraces the force's history from the medieval maréchaussée to today through uniforms, weapons, vehicles and archives.

musee-de-la-grande-guerre.name: Museum of the Great War
musee-de-la-grande-guerre.description: Opened in 2011 on the edge of the First Battle of the Marne battlefield, this museum holds one of Europe's largest First World War collections, some 70,000 objects and documents built around collector Jean-Pierre Verney's holdings.

musee-de-la-grande-loge-de-france.name: Museum of the Grande Loge de France
musee-de-la-grande-loge-de-france.description: Housed in the Grande Loge de France's headquarters, a former Franciscan convent in the 17th arrondissement, this museum of the history, symbols and art of Freemasonry preserves over 3,000 objects dating from the 18th century onwards.

musee-de-la-liberation-de-paris-musee-du.name: Museum of the Liberation of Paris
musee-de-la-liberation-de-paris-musee-du.description: Reinstalled in 2019 in the Ledoux pavilions at Denfert-Rochereau, this City of Paris museum recounts the Occupation and the liberation of Paris through General Leclerc and Jean Moulin, and includes Colonel Rol-Tanguy's underground command post of August 1944.

musee-de-la-musique.name: Music Museum
musee-de-la-musique.description: The Philharmonie de Paris's instrument museum at La Villette displays around 1,000 pieces from a collection of more than 8,000 — Stradivarius violins, harpsichords, rare guitars — covering five centuries of European and world music.

musee-de-la-poste.name: Postal Museum
musee-de-la-poste.description: The museum of the French postal service, near Montparnasse, reopened in 2019 after full renovation. Its collections range from mail coaches, uniforms and postboxes to the airmail epic and one of France's leading philatelic collections.

musee-de-la-prefecture-de-police.name: Museum of the Paris Police Prefecture
musee-de-la-prefecture-de-police.description: Tucked inside a working police station in the Latin Quarter, this museum traces the history of the Paris police from the 17th century onwards, with archives, uniforms, weapons and evidence from celebrated criminal cases.

musee-de-la-renaissance-chateau-d-ecouen.name: National Museum of the Renaissance
musee-de-la-renaissance-chateau-d-ecouen.description: France's national Renaissance museum fills the 16th-century château built for Constable Anne de Montmorency north of Paris. Its collections include the ten-piece David and Bathsheba tapestry cycle, enamels, ceramics and painted fireplaces.

musee-de-la-resistance-nationale.name: National Resistance Museum
musee-de-la-resistance-nationale.description: This museum in Champigny-sur-Marne holds one of the largest collections devoted to the French Resistance — underground newspapers, leaflets, weapons and personal effects — displayed since 2020 in the new Aimé Césaire building.

musee-de-la-toile-de-jouy.name: Toile de Jouy Museum
musee-de-la-toile-de-jouy.description: Housed in the Château de l'Églantine, this museum tells the story of toile de Jouy, the printed cottons made at the Oberkampf manufactory founded in Jouy-en-Josas in 1760, through fabrics, printing plates and period costume.

musee-de-la-vie-romantique.name: Museum of Romantic Life
musee-de-la-vie-romantique.description: The 1830 house and studio of painter Ary Scheffer, in the 'New Athens' quarter at the foot of Montmartre, evokes the Romantic era with George Sand memorabilia, works by Scheffer and his circle, and a garden tearoom.

musee-de-melun.name: Melun Museum
musee-de-melun.description: Melun's museum of art and history, founded in 1860 and housed in the 16th-century Hôtel de la Vicomté. It presents Gallo-Roman and medieval finds from the town alongside paintings and a large body of work by sculptor Henri Chapu.

musee-de-montmartre.name: Montmartre Museum
musee-de-montmartre.description: Set in one of the hill's oldest houses, where Renoir, Suzanne Valadon and Utrillo lived or worked, the museum traces Montmartre's bohemian era through paintings and cabaret posters, with Valadon's recreated studio and gardens above the Clos Montmartre vineyard.

musee-de-port-royal-des-champs.name: Museum of Port-Royal des Champs
musee-de-port-royal-des-champs.description: National museum on the site of the ruined abbey of Port-Royal-des-Champs, centre of 17th-century Jansenism linked to Pascal and Racine. The former Petites Écoles display paintings by Philippe de Champaigne and relics of the community, amid the abbey grounds.

musee-de-prehistoire-d-ile-de-france.name: Île-de-France Museum of Prehistory
musee-de-prehistoire-d-ile-de-france.description: Departmental museum of the region's prehistory, in a raw-concrete building by architect Roland Simounet on the edge of Nemours forest. Displays run from the Palaeolithic to the Iron Age, with finds from major Seine valley sites such as Pincevent and Étiolles.

musee-de-provins-et-du-provinois.name: Museum of Provins and the Provinois
musee-de-provins-et-du-provinois.description: Local museum of the medieval fair town of Provins, a UNESCO World Heritage site, housed in the Maison Romane, one of its oldest houses. Its collections span prehistory to the 19th century, from medieval sculpture and glazed floor tiles to religious treasures.

musee-de-saint-maur-villa-medicis.name: Villa Médicis – House of Arts and Culture
musee-de-saint-maur-villa-medicis.description: Saint-Maur's art and history museum, in an old house renamed 'Villa Médicis' after Catherine de' Medici's stays at the town's château. It keeps carved stones from the medieval abbey, paintings and prints, and a major collection of Art Deco ceramicist Édouard Cazaux.

musee-departemental-albert-kahn.name: Albert Kahn Museum
musee-departemental-albert-kahn.description: Museum of banker-philanthropist Albert Kahn's 'Archives of the Planet', some 72,000 early colour photographs taken around the world between 1909 and 1931. Its Kengo Kuma-designed building opens onto four hectares of gardens with Japanese, English and French scenes.

musee-departemental-maurice-denis.name: Maurice Denis Museum
musee-departemental-maurice-denis.description: Museum of painter Maurice Denis and the Nabis, in the Priory, a 17th-century former royal hospital Denis bought in 1914 and lived in until his death. It shows works by Denis, Sérusier, Bonnard and their circle, the chapel he decorated, and terraced gardens.

musee-departemental-stephane-mallarme.name: Stéphane Mallarmé Museum
musee-departemental-stephane-mallarme.description: The riverside house facing the Fontainebleau forest where poet Stéphane Mallarmé spent his summers from 1874 and died in 1898. His furnished rooms, personal belongings, portraits and manuscripts are preserved, along with a garden replanted as in his day.

musee-des-annees-trente.name: Museum of the 1930s
musee-des-annees-trente.description: Museum of art and design from the interwar years: figurative painting, sculpture, Art Deco furniture and models of the modernist villas built in Boulogne-Billancourt by Le Corbusier, Mallet-Stevens and Perret. It is part of the Espace Landowski cultural complex.

musee-des-archives-nationales-hotel-de-s.name: Museum of the National Archives – Hôtel de Soubise
musee-des-archives-nationales-hotel-de-s.description: Museum of the French National Archives in the Hôtel de Soubise, a princely Marais mansion with rococo apartments decorated by Germain Boffrand. Its rotating displays present landmark documents of French history, from royal wills to Marie-Antoinette's last letter.

musee-des-arts-asiatiques-guimet.name: Guimet Museum
musee-des-arts-asiatiques-guimet.description: France's national museum of Asian arts, founded by industrialist Émile Guimet in 1889 and holding one of the largest Asian collections outside Asia: Khmer sculpture, Chinese bronzes and porcelain, Japanese screens, Indian and Himalayan art.

musee-des-arts-decoratifs-union-centrale.name: Museum of Decorative Arts
musee-des-arts-decoratifs-union-centrale.description: Decorative arts and design museum in the Rivoli wing of the Louvre palace, covering furniture, glass, ceramics, wallpaper, graphic design and fashion from the Middle Ages to today, with period rooms and strong Art Nouveau and Art Deco holdings.

musee-des-arts-et-metiers.name: Museum of Arts and Crafts
musee-des-arts-et-metiers.description: Technology museum founded in 1794 with the Conservatoire des arts et métiers, partly housed in a former medieval priory. Its instruments, machines and vehicles include Foucault's pendulum, Lavoisier's laboratory and Ader's and Blériot's early aeroplanes.

musee-des-avelines-musee-d-art-et-d-hist.name: Musée des Avelines – Saint-Cloud Museum of Art and History
musee-des-avelines-musee-d-art-et-d-hist.description: Saint-Cloud's museum of art and history, in a 1930s villa inspired by the Villa Kérylos. Its collections recall the royal château that burned in 1870, the town's 18th-century soft-paste porcelain manufactory, and local painters and sculptors.

musee-des-monnaies-et-medailles.name: Museum of the Monnaie de Paris (11 Conti)
musee-des-monnaies-et-medailles.description: Museum of the Monnaie de Paris — the French mint, founded in 864 — inside its 18th-century neoclassical palace on the Quai de Conti. The '11 Conti' circuit displays coins, medals and presses, and looks into workshops where craftsmen still strike medals today.

musee-des-monuments-francais.name: Museum of French Monuments
musee-des-monuments-francais.description: Within the Cité de l'architecture et du patrimoine at the Palais de Chaillot, this museum conceived by Viollet-le-Duc assembles life-size casts of portals and sculpture from French cathedrals and châteaux, together with copies of medieval wall paintings.

musee-des-pays-de-seine-et-marne.name: Museum of the Seine-et-Marne Countryside
musee-des-pays-de-seine-et-marne.description: Departmental museum of rural life in Seine-et-Marne: farm tools, trades and popular traditions of the Brie countryside, with a section devoted to the writer Pierre Mac Orlan, who lived in Saint-Cyr-sur-Morin until his death in 1970.

musee-des-plans-reliefs.name: Museum of Relief Maps
musee-des-plans-reliefs.description: Under the roof of the Hôtel des Invalides, this museum preserves the collection of relief maps of fortified towns begun for Louis XIV in 1668: minutely detailed scale models once used to plan sieges and defences along France's frontiers.

musee-des-transports-urbains-interurbain.name: Museum of Urban, Interurban and Rural Transport (AMTUIR)
musee-des-transports-urbains-interurbain.description: Volunteer-run museum of the AMTUIR association preserving over a century of French public transport: horse-drawn omnibuses, trams, trolleybuses, buses and metro cars kept in a large depot in Chelles, shown during open days and heritage events.

musee-du-chateau.name: Dourdan Castle Museum
musee-du-chateau.description: Museum inside the château of Dourdan, a well-preserved fortress built around 1220 for King Philip Augustus and long used as a prison. Its collections cover the castle's history, local archaeology and medieval pottery.

musee-du-domaine-royal-de-marly-louvecie.name: Museum of the Royal Estate of Marly – Louveciennes / Marly-le-Roi
musee-du-domaine-royal-de-marly-louvecie.description: Museum devoted to the vanished royal estate of Marly, Louis XIV's retreat from Versailles. Paintings, sculptures and models evoke the demolished château, its gardens and the famous Marly machine that raised Seine water to the fountains.

musee-du-jouet-pierre-pinel.name: Pierre Pinel Toy Museum
musee-du-jouet-pierre-pinel.description: Toy museum set in the fortified 14th-century gatehouse of Poissy's former royal priory, founded by Philip the Fair. Some 800 French toys from 1850 to 1950 include porcelain dolls, teddy bears, rocking horses and electric trains.

musee-du-louvre.name: The Louvre
musee-du-louvre.description: The world's largest art museum, housed in the former palace of the French kings. Its collections run from antiquity to 1848, from Egyptian antiquities and the Venus de Milo to the Mona Lisa, entered beneath I. M. Pei's glass pyramid.

musee-du-moyen-age-thermes-et-hotel-de-c.name: Cluny Museum – National Museum of the Middle Ages
musee-du-moyen-age-thermes-et-hotel-de-c.description: France's national museum of the Middle Ages, set in the Gallo-Roman baths of Lutetia and the 15th-century Hôtel de Cluny. Medieval sculpture, stained glass and goldwork surround the celebrated Lady and the Unicorn tapestries.

musee-du-parfum-fragonard.name: Fragonard Perfume Museum
musee-du-parfum-fragonard.description: Museum of the Grasse perfume house Fragonard, in a Napoleon III townhouse near the Opéra Garnier. Copper stills, essences and antique flacons trace three thousand years of perfume-making, from ancient Egypt to modern extraction techniques.

musee-du-quai-branly-jacques-chirac.name: Quai Branly Museum – Jacques Chirac
musee-du-quai-branly-jacques-chirac.description: Museum of the arts and civilisations of Africa, Asia, Oceania and the Americas, opened in 2006 in a Jean Nouvel building beside the Seine. Its collection of some 370,000 objects includes masks, textiles and ritual sculpture.

musee-du-service-de-sante-des-armees-du-.name: Museum of the Army Health Service at Val-de-Grâce
musee-du-service-de-sante-des-armees-du-.description: Museum of French military medicine, set in the cloister of the 17th-century royal abbey of Val-de-Grâce founded by Anne of Austria. Instruments, uniforms and field equipment trace the care of soldiers from the Ancien Régime to today.

musee-dunoyer-de-segonzac.name: Dunoyer de Segonzac Museum
musee-dunoyer-de-segonzac.description: Small municipal museum honouring painter and engraver André Dunoyer de Segonzac (1884-1974), born in Boussy-Saint-Antoine. It holds etchings, lithographs, posters, photographs and books largely from the artist's own library.

musee-emile-jean.name: Émile Jean Museum
musee-emile-jean.description: Local history museum founded in 1973 by the historical society of Villiers-sur-Marne, in a 19th-century house. Documents, photographs and everyday objects recreate life in the Brie region, from village school days to the war of 1870.

musee-eugene-delacroix.name: Eugène Delacroix Museum
musee-eugene-delacroix.description: The last home and studio of Romantic painter Eugène Delacroix, on the quiet place de Furstenberg, where he lived from 1857 until his death in 1863. Paintings, drawings and personal memorabilia are shown in his apartment and garden studio.

musee-fragonard.name: Fragonard Museum
musee-fragonard.description: One of France's oldest museums, created in 1766 within the Alfort veterinary school. Its anatomy and pathology collections culminate in Honoré Fragonard's 18th-century flayed figures, including his famous horseman of the Apocalypse.

musee-francais-de-la-carte-a-jouer-et-ga.name: French Playing Card Museum
musee-francais-de-la-carte-a-jouer-et-ga.description: The only museum in France devoted to playing cards, with historic decks, tarots and engraving plates from around the world. An adjoining gallery recounts the history of Issy-les-Moulineaux and its vanished château.

musee-gustave-moreau.name: Gustave Moreau Museum
musee-gustave-moreau.description: House and studio of Symbolist painter Gustave Moreau, arranged as a museum by the artist himself before his death in 1898. Thousands of his paintings, watercolours and drawings hang floor to ceiling around a spiral staircase.

musee-henri-chapu.name: Henri Chapu Museum
musee-henri-chapu.description: Museum in sculptor Henri Chapu's native village, created in 1887 with works he gave to Le Mée-sur-Seine. More than sixty plaster models and bronzes trace the career of this leading official sculptor of 19th-century France.

musee-jardin-paul-landowski.name: Paul Landowski Garden Museum
musee-jardin-paul-landowski.description: Garden museum on the site of the Boulogne studio of Paul Landowski, sculptor of Rio de Janeiro's Christ the Redeemer. Around a hundred sculptures and models are displayed in the garden and two underground galleries.

musee-jean-jacques-henner.name: Jean-Jacques Henner Museum
musee-jean-jacques-henner.description: National museum devoted to Alsatian painter Jean-Jacques Henner (1829-1905), in a Plaine Monceau townhouse that belonged to fellow painter Guillaume Dubufe. It displays Henner's portraits, landscapes and idealised nudes.

musee-jean-jacques-rousseau.name: Jean-Jacques Rousseau Museum
musee-jean-jacques-rousseau.description: The modest Mont-Louis house in Montmorency where Jean-Jacques Rousseau lived from 1757 to 1762 and wrote Julie, Émile and The Social Contract. Period rooms and the garden pavilion evoke the philosopher's daily life.

musee-lambinet.name: Lambinet Museum
musee-lambinet.description: Versailles's municipal museum, set in an elegant 18th-century townhouse, with period interiors, fine and decorative arts, and collections on the city's history, notably the French Revolution.

musee-librairie-du-compagnonnage.name: Compagnonnage Museum and Bookshop
musee-librairie-du-compagnonnage.description: Small museum of the compagnons du Tour de France craft guilds, displaying masterpieces made by journeymen — model staircases and works in wood, stone and iron — alongside a bookshop devoted to the guild tradition.

musee-municipal.name: Moret-sur-Loing Municipal Museum
musee-municipal.description: Local history museum of Moret-sur-Loing, the fortified medieval town on the Loing where Alfred Sisley spent his final years; its collection of over 1,400 objects retraces the town's past and notable figures.

musee-municipal-91150.name: Étampes Intercommunal Museum
musee-municipal-91150.description: Founded in 1875 beside the town hall, this museum covers the Étampes region from fossils and medieval archaeology to 19th-century works by local artists such as sculptor Élias Robert and painter Narcisse Berchère.

musee-municipal-d-art-et-d-histoire.name: Colombes Municipal Museum of Art and History
musee-municipal-d-art-et-d-histoire.description: Municipal museum tracing the history of Colombes, from Gallo-Roman archaeology and the 17th-century estate of Henrietta of England to local industries such as Hispano-Suiza and the Olympic stadium of the 1924 Games.

musee-municipal-ducastel-vera-de-saint-g.name: Ducastel-Vera Municipal Museum of Saint-Germain-en-Laye
musee-municipal-ducastel-vera-de-saint-g.description: Saint-Germain-en-Laye's municipal collection, born of Louis-Alexandre Ducastel's 1872 bequest: nearly 9,000 works from Egyptian antiquity to the 20th century, including fine 18th-century pastels and a preserved royal apothecary.

musee-municipal-robert-dubois-corneau.name: Robert Dubois-Corneau Municipal Museum
musee-municipal-robert-dubois-corneau.description: Housed in the former home of collector Robert Dubois-Corneau, this museum tells the story of Brunoy and the Yerres valley through paintings, prints and objets d'art from the 18th century to the present day.

musee-national-de-l-histoire-et-des-cult.name: National Museum of the History of Immigration
musee-national-de-l-histoire-et-des-cult.description: France's national museum of immigration history, housed in the Art Deco Palais de la Porte Dorée built for the 1931 Colonial Exhibition; collections and personal testimonies trace two centuries of migration to France.

musee-national-de-la-legion-d-honneur-et.name: National Museum of the Legion of Honour and Orders of Chivalry
musee-national-de-la-legion-d-honneur-et.description: Set in the Hôtel de Salm opposite the Musée d'Orsay, this museum displays decorations, insignia and paintings tracing the Legion of Honour, founded by Napoleon in 1802, and orders of chivalry from France and abroad.

musee-national-de-la-marine.name: National Maritime Museum
musee-national-de-la-marine.description: One of the world's oldest maritime museums, at the Palais de Chaillot, tracing French naval history through ship models, paintings, figureheads and instruments, from the age of sail to modern seafaring.

musee-national-des-chateaux-de-malmaison.name: National Museum of the Châteaux of Malmaison and Bois-Préau
musee-national-des-chateaux-de-malmaison.description: The country residence of Napoleon and Empress Joséphine, who lived at Malmaison until her death in 1814; the château preserves its Consulate-era interiors, imperial furnishings and personal mementoes, set in a rose-filled park.

musee-national-des-chateaux-de-versaille.name: Palace of Versailles
musee-national-des-chateaux-de-versaille.description: The vast royal palace of Louis XIV and his successors, a UNESCO World Heritage site, with the Hall of Mirrors, the State Apartments, the Trianon palaces and formal gardens designed by Le Nôtre.

musee-national-du-chateau-de-fontaineble.name: Palace of Fontainebleau
musee-national-du-chateau-de-fontaineble.description: A residence of French sovereigns for eight centuries, from the Capetians to Napoleon III; the palace preserves exceptional Renaissance interiors created for François I, Napoleon's apartments and extensive gardens, a UNESCO World Heritage site.

musee-nissim-de-camondo-union-centrale-d.name: Nissim de Camondo Museum
musee-nissim-de-camondo-union-centrale-d.description: The mansion of Count Moïse de Camondo, built in 1911–1914 and kept as he left it, houses his outstanding collection of 18th-century French furniture and decorative arts; it is named for his son Nissim, killed in World War I.

musee-picasso.name: Picasso Museum
musee-picasso.description: The world's largest public collection of Picasso's work — paintings, sculptures, drawings and the artist's personal archives — displayed in the Hôtel Salé, a grand 17th-century mansion in the Marais.

musee-pissarro.name: Pissarro-Pontoise Museum of Art and History (MAHPP)
musee-pissarro.description: Museum on the heights of Pontoise devoted to Camille Pissarro, who painted the town for nearly two decades; it holds prints and drawings by the Impressionist master along with works by painters of the Oise valley.

musee-rambolitrain.name: Rambolitrain Museum
musee-rambolitrain.description: Museum of toy and model trains in Rambouillet, with more than 4,000 pieces from the 19th century onward and a large working miniature railway that retraces the history of rail travel.

musee-rodin.name: Rodin Museum
musee-rodin.description: Museum devoted to sculptor Auguste Rodin in the 18th-century Hôtel Biron, where he lived and worked; The Thinker, The Kiss and The Gates of Hell are shown in the mansion and its large sculpture garden.

musee-rodin-meudon.name: Rodin Museum, Meudon
musee-rodin-meudon.description: The Villa des Brillants in Meudon was Rodin's home and main studio; plaster casts and studies reveal the sculptor's working process, and his tomb in the garden is crowned by a cast of The Thinker.

musee-roybet-fould.name: Roybet-Fould Museum
musee-roybet-fould.description: Courbevoie's municipal museum, set in the wooden Sweden and Norway pavilion built for the 1878 World's Fair and re-erected in Bécon park. It keeps 19th-century paintings by Ferdinand Roybet and Consuelo Fould, along with works by the sculptor Jean-Baptiste Carpeaux.

musee-victor-aubert.name: Victor Aubert Museum
musee-victor-aubert.description: A small local-history museum housed in the remains of an 11th-century Benedictine priory beside Maule's church. Founded by self-taught archaeologist Victor Aubert, it displays fossils, prehistoric and Merovingian finds, and the rural folk traditions of the area.

musee-yves-saint-laurent-paris.name: Yves Saint Laurent Museum, Paris
musee-yves-saint-laurent-paris.description: The historic couture house at 5 avenue Marceau where Yves Saint Laurent created his collections from 1974 to 2002, now a museum devoted to his work, holding haute couture garments, sketches and the designer's studio preserved as it was.

musee-zadkine.name: Zadkine Museum
musee-zadkine.description: The house and studios near the Luxembourg Gardens where Russian-born sculptor Ossip Zadkine lived and worked from 1928 to 1967. This City of Paris museum shows his carvings and bronzes in the workshops and a small sculpture garden.

musee-zola-dreyfus.name: Zola-Dreyfus Museum
musee-zola-dreyfus.description: Émile Zola's country house in Médan, where he wrote much of the Rougon-Macquart cycle, paired with the first museum devoted to the Dreyfus Affair, recalling the writer's "J'accuse...!" and his fight for the captain's rehabilitation.

museum-national-d-histoire-naturelle.name: National Museum of Natural History
museum-national-d-histoire-naturelle.description: France's national natural history museum, founded in 1793 in the Jardin des Plantes. Its galleries range from the Grande Galerie de l'Évolution to vast collections of paleontology, comparative anatomy, mineralogy and botany.

palais-galliera-musee-de-la-mode-et-de-l.name: Palais Galliera, Fashion Museum of the City of Paris
palais-galliera-musee-de-la-mode-et-de-l.description: The City of Paris fashion museum, housed in a 19th-century Renaissance-style palace near the Trocadéro. Its collections trace clothing from the 18th century to the present, haute couture included, shown through rotating displays and exhibitions.

pantheon.name: Panthéon
pantheon.description: A neoclassical monument on the Montagne Sainte-Geneviève, built as a church by Soufflot and turned into the resting place of great French figures — Voltaire, Hugo, Zola and Marie Curie among them. Foucault's pendulum swings beneath its dome.

petit-palais-musee-des-beaux-arts-de-la-.name: Petit Palais, City of Paris Fine Arts Museum
petit-palais-musee-des-beaux-arts-de-la-.description: Built by Charles Girault for the 1900 World's Fair, the fine arts museum of the City of Paris displays paintings, sculpture and decorative arts from antiquity to 1914 — Rembrandt, Monet and Courbet among them — around a garden courtyard.

sainte-chapelle.name: Sainte-Chapelle
sainte-chapelle.description: The Gothic royal chapel on the Île de la Cité, built in the 1240s by Louis IX to house the relics of the Passion. Its upper chapel is ringed by fifteen monumental 13th-century stained-glass windows.

tours-de-notre-dame-de-paris.name: Towers of Notre-Dame de Paris
tours-de-notre-dame-de-paris.description: The medieval towers of Notre-Dame Cathedral, reopened after the post-fire restoration. The climb passes the gallery of chimeras and the belfry of the great bell Emmanuel before reaching a panorama over the Seine and central Paris.

villa-savoye.name: Villa Savoye
villa-savoye.description: Le Corbusier's modernist villa of 1928–1931 in Poissy, a manifesto of his "five points of architecture" with its pilotis, ribbon windows and roof garden. It is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage site.

cite-internationale-de-la-langue-francai.name: International City of the French Language at the Château de Villers-Cotterêts
cite-internationale-de-la-langue-francai.description: A Renaissance château built by François I from 1532, where the 1539 ordinance mandating French in the kingdom's administrative and judicial acts was signed. Restored and converted into the Cité internationale de la langue française, it reopened in 2023 with a permanent exhibition on the history of French and the Francophone world.

cloitre-de-la-cathedrale-de-bayonne.name: Cloister of Bayonne Cathedral
cloitre-de-la-cathedrale-de-bayonne.description: A 14th-century Gothic rayonnant cloister adjoining the south side of Bayonne's Sainte-Marie Cathedral, one of the largest in France. Its galleries hold tomb recesses and funerary slabs from the 14th to 18th centuries and once served as a meeting place for guilds and neighbourhood assemblies.

cloitre-de-la-cathedrale-de-frejus.name: Cloister of Fréjus Cathedral
cloitre-de-la-cathedrale-de-frejus.description: A two-tiered Romanesque cloister of the 12th century beside Fréjus's Saint-Léonce Cathedral, its upper gallery carried on slender 13th-century Corinthian columns. Its ceiling preserves more than three hundred wooden panels painted in the 14th and 15th centuries with figures, animals and fantastical creatures.

cloitre-de-la-psalette.name: Cloister of the Psalette in Tours
cloitre-de-la-psalette.description: The chapter cloister of Tours Cathedral (Saint-Gatien), its oldest gallery dating from 1442 and combining Gothic and Renaissance work. It housed the psalette, the canons' choir school and scriptorium, and its northeast corner holds a carved spiral staircase reminiscent of the one at the Château de Blois.

colonne-de-la-grande-armee-a-wimille.name: Grande Armée Column at Wimille
colonne-de-la-grande-armee-a-wimille.description: A 54-metre neoclassical column raised at Wimille between 1804 and 1841, funded by the soldiers of the Grande Armée whom Napoleon had gathered at the Camp de Boulogne for a planned invasion of England. Construction stalled after the Empire's fall and resumed under the July Monarchy; the column is topped by a statue of Napoleon.

crypte-et-tour-de-la-cathedrale-de-bourg.name: Crypt and Tower of Bourges Cathedral
crypte-et-tour-de-la-cathedrale-de-bourg.description: Beneath the choir of Bourges Cathedral, the lower church and its Romanesque crypt, built between 1195 and 1206 to offset the slope of the ground, hold the kneeling effigies of the Duke and Duchess of Berry. The north tower, rebuilt between 1508 and 1542 after its 1506 collapse, rises 65 metres above the cathedral, a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1992.

domaine-national-de-saint-cloud.name: National Estate of Saint-Cloud
domaine-national-de-saint-cloud.description: A former royal and imperial château above the Seine, given by Louis XIV to his brother Philippe d'Orléans in 1658 and laid out with gardens by Le Nôtre; Napoleon I was proclaimed emperor there in 1804. Burned by a shell during the 1870 siege of Paris and later razed, the château itself is gone, but its 460-hectare park, with the Grande Cascade and formal gardens, survives as a national estate.

domaine-national-du-palais-royal.name: Palais-Royal
domaine-national-du-palais-royal.description: A palace built from 1628 by Cardinal Richelieu, who bequeathed it to Louis XIII in 1636; Anne of Austria and the young Louis XIV lived there during the Fronde. Passed to the House of Orléans in 1692, it gained Victor Louis's arcaded galleries in the 1780s, once a fashionable hub of Parisian life, and its garden has held Daniel Buren's striped columns since 1986.

ensemble-cathedral-du-puy-en-velay.name: Le Puy Cathedral Complex
ensemble-cathedral-du-puy-en-velay.description: A Romanesque cathedral of the 11th–13th centuries built of polychrome volcanic stone on a Byzantine-inspired plan, the historic starting point of the Via Podiensis pilgrim route to Compostela and a place of pilgrimage to its Black Virgin since the Middle Ages. The complex includes a 12th-century Romanesque cloister with carved capitals and a freestanding 56-metre bell tower; it has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1998.

enserune-oppidum-et-musee-archeologique.name: Ensérune Oppidum and Archaeological Museum
enserune-oppidum-et-musee-archeologique.description: Gaulish hilltop settlement continuously occupied from the 6th century BC to the 1st century AD, on a hill between Béziers and Narbonne, one of the most important pre-Roman sites in southern France. Rediscovered in the 19th century and excavated since the early 20th, it yielded a necropolis of nearly 500 graves; the museum displays Greek and Iberian vases along with Celtic weapons found on site.

fort-saint-andre-a-villeneuve-lez-avigno.name: Fort Saint-André
fort-saint-andre-a-villeneuve-lez-avigno.description: Fortress built on Mont Andaon under King Jean II the Good and completed under Charles V by architect Jean de Loubières, who also built the Palais des Papes in Avignon, to assert French royal power across the Rhône from papal Avignon. Its 750-metre wall, twin-towered gatehouse and Tour des Masques still dominate Villeneuve-lès-Avignon, alongside the neighbouring Benedictine abbey.

forteresse-de-salses.name: Fortress of Salses
forteresse-de-salses.description: Fortress built between 1497 and 1503 by the Catholic Monarchs Ferdinand of Aragon and Isabella of Castile to seal the passage between Languedoc and Roussillon on the frontier of the kingdom of France. Semi-buried, with walls 6 to 10 metres thick and four corner towers, it marks the transition from medieval military architecture to flat-trajectory artillery fire; captured by French troops in 1639, it lost its strategic role after the 1659 Treaty of the Pyrenees.

grotte-de-pair-non-pair.name: Pair-non-Pair Cave
grotte-de-pair-non-pair.description: Painted cave discovered in 1881 by the self-taught local scholar François Daleau, who excavated over 15,000 flint, bone and ivory tools there until 1887. Its engravings, dated to the Aurignacian period between 37,000 and 32,000 years ago and including a giant deer and a 2.5-metre horse, are among the oldest known and helped establish the authenticity of prehistoric art.

hotel-de-sade.name: Hôtel de Sade
hotel-de-sade.description: Mansion built in 1513 by Balthazar de Sade, an ancestor of the Marquis de Sade, combining flamboyant Gothic and Renaissance styles in the centre of Saint-Rémy-de-Provence. Acquired by the state in 1929, it has housed the archaeological museum since 1954, displaying finds from the nearby Roman site of Glanum alongside remains of 4th-century Roman baths and a 16th-century chapel.

hotel-de-sully.name: Hôtel de Sully
hotel-de-sully.description: Mansion built between 1625 and 1630 in the Marais by architect Jean Androuet du Cerceau for the financier Mesme Gallet, then bought in 1634 by Maximilien de Béthune, Duke of Sully, who had its interior decorated. Its courtyard and garden façades, adorned with allegorical reliefs of the Seasons and Elements, rank among the finest examples of Louis XIII style; restored, it has housed the headquarters of the Centre des monuments nationaux since 1967.

maison-d-ernest-renan-a-treguier.name: Ernest Renan's House
maison-d-ernest-renan-a-treguier.description: Half-timbered house in Tréguier where the writer and philosopher Ernest Renan was born in 1823 and lived until he was fifteen. Donated to the state by his granddaughters, it is now a museum displaying period Breton furniture, a reconstruction of his office at the Collège de France, and mementos of his sister Henriette.

maison-de-george-sand-a-nohant.name: George Sand's House
maison-de-george-sand-a-nohant.description: 18th-century château in the Berry region, inherited by George Sand in 1821 and where she settled permanently in 1853 after hosting Chopin, Liszt, Balzac, Flaubert and Delacroix; she died there in 1876. The house preserves her furniture, natural history collections, and the puppet theatre created by her son Maurice in 1847.

maison-de-georges-clemenceau-a-saint-vin.name: Georges Clemenceau's House
maison-de-georges-clemenceau-a-saint-vin.description: Traditional Vendée farmhouse facing the Atlantic at Saint-Vincent-sur-Jard, where Georges Clemenceau retired after his defeat in the 1920 presidential election and lived until his death in 1929. The museum preserves his furniture and belongings, including Japanese diplomatic gifts, along with an impressionist-style garden inspired by his friend Claude Monet's garden at Giverny.

monastere-de-saorge.name: Monastery of Saorge
monastere-de-saorge.description: Franciscan monastery founded in 1633 above the hilltop village of Saorge, in the upper Roya valley. Its four-gallery cloister preserves 18th-century frescoes depicting the life of Saint Francis, and the monastery, bought by the state in 1967, has hosted a writers' residency since 2001.

monastere-royal-de-brou-a-bourg-en-bress.name: Royal Monastery of Brou, Bourg-en-Bresse
monastere-royal-de-brou-a-bourg-en-bress.description: Monastic complex built from 1506 by Margaret of Austria to house the tomb of her husband Philibert the Fair, in the Flamboyant Gothic style of Brabant architect Louis van Bodeghem. The church of Saint-Nicolas-de-Tolentin holds the sculpted tombs of Margaret of Austria, Philibert the Fair and Margaret of Bourbon, while the three cloisters now house the Musée de Brou.

palais-du-tau-a-reims.name: Palace of Tau, Reims
palais-du-tau-a-reims.description: Former residence of the archbishops of Reims, remodeled in classical style by Robert de Cotte in the late 17th century, the palace hosted the coronation banquets of French kings in its Salle du Tau. A museum since 1972, it displays original statues from the cathedral — including a 5.4-metre Goliath — tapestries, and the coronation treasury, among them Charlemagne's talisman.

palais-jacques-c-ur.name: Palace of Jacques Cœur
palais-jacques-c-ur.description: Residence built between 1443 and 1451 for Jacques Cœur, a wealthy merchant ennobled by Charles VII, in a Flamboyant Gothic style anticipating the Renaissance. Four wings arranged around a courtyard hold carved fireplaces, a chapel decorated with his coat of arms, and eight spiral staircases carved with the shells and hearts that were his emblem.

site-archeologique-de-glanum.name: Archaeological Site of Glanum
site-archeologique-de-glanum.description: Ancient city occupied from the 6th century BCE to the 3rd century CE, where a Celto-Ligurian sanctuary built around a healing spring gave way to a Hellenistic settlement influenced by Marseille and then a prosperous Roman town under Augustus. The site preserves a forum, baths, peristyle houses and, at its entrance, the Mausoleum of the Julii and a triumphal arch, together known as Les Antiques.

site-des-megalithes-de-locmariaquer.name: Locmariaquer Megaliths
site-des-megalithes-de-locmariaquer.description: Megalithic complex built between 5000 and 3800 BCE, comprising the Grand Menhir Brisé — a granite block over 20 metres long, the largest known standing stone in Europe, now broken into four pieces — the Table des Marchands dolmen and the 140-metre Er Grah tumulus. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2025 together with the Carnac megaliths.

site-gallo-romain-de-sanxay.name: Gallo-Roman Site of Sanxay
site-gallo-romain-de-sanxay.description: A vast Gallo-Roman sanctuary devoted to the cult of healing waters, active from the 1st to the 2nd century, centred on a temple with an octagonal cella ringed by a cross-shaped portico, an 89-metre theatre seating close to 6,600 spectators, and a bath complex. Uncovered by Father Camille de La Croix between 1881 and 1883, the sanctuary covers some twenty hectares in the Vonne valley.

sites-et-musee-archeologiques-de-montmau.name: Montmaurin Archaeological Sites and Museum
sites-et-musee-archeologiques-de-montmau.description: The Montmaurin museum traces 400,000 years of human occupation, from the Coupe-Gorge cave — where human remains some 200,000 years old and a cave lion skeleton were unearthed — to the Gallo-Roman villa of Lassalles, a vast agricultural estate transformed in the 4th century into a 5,800-square-metre palace with two peristyles, baths and a hexagonal Gallic temple.

sites-prehistoriques-de-la-vallee-de-la-.name: Prehistoric Sites of the Vézère Valley
sites-prehistoriques-de-la-vallee-de-la-.description: The Centre des monuments nationaux manages seven of the sites inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1979 in the Vézère valley: the decorated caves of Font-de-Gaume and Les Combarelles, the carved Abri du Poisson, the sculpted animal frieze at Cap Blanc, and the Mousterian deposits of Le Moustier, La Micoque and La Ferrassie. Together they document human occupation from the Middle to the Upper Palaeolithic, from Mousterian to Magdalenian times.

tour-pey-berland-a-bordeaux.name: Pey-Berland Tower, Bordeaux
tour-pey-berland-a-bordeaux.description: Gothic bell tower standing apart from Bordeaux's Saint-André Cathedral, built between 1440 and 1500 at the initiative of Archbishop Pey Berland so its bells would not shake the adjoining building. From the top of the 66-metre tower, reached by 233 steps, a panorama opens over Bordeaux; the site is a UNESCO World Heritage listing as part of the Routes of Santiago de Compostela.

tours-de-la-cathedrale-de-reims.name: Towers of Reims Cathedral
tours-de-la-cathedrale-de-reims.description: The western towers of Reims Cathedral, the Gothic building where French kings were crowned from 1027 to 1825 and now a UNESCO World Heritage site, rise about 81.5 metres and were completed around 1275. The climb reaches their summit, past the remains of bells melted in the 1914 fire, for a panorama over the city.

tours-de-la-rochelle.name: Towers of La Rochelle
tours-de-la-rochelle.description: Three medieval towers guard the entrance to La Rochelle's old harbour: the 14th-century Tour Saint-Nicolas and Tour de la Chaîne, once linked by a chain that closed off the port. The Tour de la Lanterne, begun in the late 12th century, later served as a prison for privateers and then for the military; more than 600 graffiti carved by inmates survive inside.

tours-et-remparts-d-aigues-mortes.name: Towers and Ramparts of Aigues-Mortes
tours-et-remparts-d-aigues-mortes.description: The ramparts encircling Aigues-Mortes, 1,640 metres long with 15 towers and 10 gates, were built between 1272 and the late 13th century under Philippe III and then Philippe IV the Fair. The Tour de Constance, built by Saint Louis (Louis IX) between 1240 and 1249, became a prison for Protestant women after 1685; Marie Durand was held there for 38 years, from 1730 to 1768.

tours-et-tresor-de-la-cathedrale-d-amien.name: Towers and Treasury of Amiens Cathedral
tours-et-tresor-de-la-cathedrale-d-amien.description: Amiens Cathedral, begun in 1220 under architect Robert de Luzarches, is the largest Gothic building in France by volume and rises to 112.70 metres; it has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1981. The visit climbs 307 steps to the top of the north tower and takes in the treasury, built up since 1206 around the relic of the head of Saint John the Baptist brought back from the Fourth Crusade.

trophee-d-auguste-a-la-turbie.name: Trophy of Augustus at La Turbie
trophee-d-auguste-a-la-turbie.description: Erected in 6 BC on the Via Julia Augusta to celebrate Augustus's subjugation of some fifty Alpine tribes, the Trophy of the Alps originally stood 50 metres tall, with a 38-metre square base topped by a colonnaded rotunda of 24 columns and a conical roof bearing the emperor's statue. Turned into a watchtower in the Middle Ages, the monument was restored in the 1930s with funding from American philanthropist Edward Tuck and reopened in 1934.

tresor-de-la-cathedrale-d-autun.name: Treasury of Autun Cathedral
tresor-de-la-cathedrale-d-autun.description: Built in the 12th century to house the relics of Saint Lazarus, brought to Autun in 972, Autun Cathedral is renowned for its west tympanum of the Last Judgement, carved by Gislebertus and signed "Gislebertus hoc fecit". Its treasury, housed in a building erected around 1520 by Bishop Jacques Hurault, brings together reliquaries, gold and silver work and liturgical vestments, dispersed during the Revolution and rebuilt as a collection in the 19th century.

tresor-de-la-cathedrale-de-lyon.name: Treasury of Lyon Cathedral
tresor-de-la-cathedrale-de-lyon.description: Lyon's Saint-Jean Cathedral, built between 1175 and 1481 in a style blending Romanesque and Gothic, houses one of the oldest working astronomical clocks, dating from the 14th century. Its treasury, assembled in the 19th century by cardinals Fesch and de Bonald in the adjoining manécanterie, brings together goldwork, Limoges enamels, tapestries and liturgical vestments from the 10th to the 19th century, including a monstrance donated by Joséphine de Beauharnais.

villa-cavrois.name: Villa Cavrois
villa-cavrois.description: Modernist villa built in Croix between 1929 and 1932 by architect Robert Mallet-Stevens for textile magnate Paul Cavrois, its 60-metre length combines reinforced concrete, steel and glass, with a 27-metre swimming pool and materials such as Swedish green marble. Abandoned and vandalised after 1987, listed as a historic monument in 1990, it was acquired by the State and restored before reopening to the public in 2015.

village-fortifie-mont-dauphin.name: Fortified Village of Mont-Dauphin
village-fortifie-mont-dauphin.description: Fortress town designed by Vauban and built from 1693 on a rocky spur 1,050 metres high, at the confluence of the Guil and Durance valleys, to protect the kingdom from incursions by the Duke of Savoy. Its pink marble ramparts, barracks, sentry turrets, arsenal and powder magazine were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 2008 as part of the Fortifications of Vauban; about 170 people still live in the village.
